title: Planning took over 14 days to return 91 sets of revised plans

beats.text: This is an investigative lead about how long San Francisco took to review revised plans.

visual.sub: Ninety-one completed review rounds exceeded the fourteen-day target

beats.text: In 337 completed rounds, the clock started when Planning received a revision.
Ninety-one ran beyond the fourteen-day target. The median still came in at thirteen days.
The analysis excluded 51 flagged rows, including missing letters and duplicate receipts.

visual.kicker: The source flags and alternative endings change the denominator

beats.text: It also excluded proxy closure dates. Each counted round ended with an actual letter.

visual.kicker: The source flags and alternative endings change the denominator

beats.text: One revision took 98 days to reach a letter. Another took 82 days and the project was later approved.

visual.kicker: One 98-day review and an 82-day review have different eventual project statuses

beats.text: On another project, the first round took fourteen days. The second took nine.
Between them, 157 days passed before the next revised plans arrived.

visual.kicker: Between two rounds, a 157-day gap preceded the next revision

beats.text: The records show those dates. They do not assign those 157 days to the applicant or the City.

visual.kicker: Between two rounds, a 157-day gap preceded the next revision
visual.text: The limits of the timing record

beats.text: A lead is a question, not an accusation.
